'''Multidimensional interpolation''' is the process of finding a multivariable function $f(x_1,\cdots,x_m)$ that for a definite set of datapoints $\{(x_1,\cdots,x_m,y)_i| i\in [0,n], i \in \mathbb{N}\}$ satisfies $f(x_1,\cdots,x_m)_i=y_i$.
<!-- Consider spelling the evaluation point out, e.g. $f(x_{1,i},\cdots,x_{m,i}) = y_i$, rather than subscripting the whole tuple: as written, the $i$ on $f(\cdots)$ first reads as an index on the function itself. -->

== Methods ==

=== Grid interpolation ===

If we know a "grid" of $n^m$ datapoints, i.e.,

$$
\{(x_{1,i_1},\cdots,x_{m,i_m},y_{i_1,\cdots,i_m})| i_1,\cdots,i_m \in [0,n-1],\, i_1,\cdots,i_m \in \mathbb{N}\}
$$

Then an $m$-dimensional interpolation can be obtained via $n^{m-1}$ one-dimensional interpolations on each variable, fixing all other variables at all possible combinations of known constant values.
<!-- Worth stating the total: $m\,n^{m-1}$ one-dimensional interpolations in all. -->
